_readme: Sets that come out of another set's packs but are FILED SEPARATELY by the
card databases this site reads, so they are absent from that set's guide.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Three of the 28 English guides were answering a
different question from the one a reader was asking. /sets/shining-fates.html
named Skyla at $11.35 as the chase card, which is true of the 73 cards the
guide holds and badly wrong about the product a reader is deciding whether to
buy: the Shiny Vault is the entire reason anyone opens Shining Fates. Same
shape on Crown Zenith, where the guide named a $44.44 Pikachu and the
Galarian Gallery sits beside it unmentioned above the fold.
The three lines below are the whole list, established on August 19, 2026 by
comparing public/data/sets.json against public/data/expansions.json three
ways and reading every candidate by hand:
by apiId prefix   an expansion whose id extends one of our 28
by name prefix    an expansion whose name starts with one of our 28
by release date   an expansion released the same day as one of our 28
That turned up five candidates and two of them are NOT companions:
svp   Scarlet & Violet Black Star Promos. Flagged promo in
expansions.json, spans the whole era rather than one set, and is
not in a Scarlet & Violet pack.
sve   Scarlet & Violet Energies. Eight basic Energy cards sold as their
own thing. Scarlet & Violet already carries its own basic Energy on
the checklist, at #257 and #258, so this is a second product and not
a missing part of that one.
THE MAP IS WRITTEN OUT RATHER THAN DERIVED, and the apiId prefix rule above
is exactly why. It also matches sv3pt5 to sv3, sv4pt5 to sv4, sv6pt5 to sv6,
sv8pt5 to sv8, me2pt5 to me2 and sv10 to sv1, and every one of those is a
mainline set with a full guide of its own. A rule that files 151 as a subset
of Obsidian Flames is worse than no rule.
Every field here is checkable against a file in this repo, and
build-set-pages.mjs re-checks the two that carry a number on EVERY BUILD
rather than trusting them:
apiId, name, cards       public/data/expansions.json (api.pokemontcg.io)
numbering, rarities      public/data/printings/*.json (TCGdex, written by
scripts/sync-all-printings.mjs)
A drift in the card count FAILS THE BUILD. The count is printed on three
pages in a sentence saying what is not counted, so a stale one makes the
correction itself a wrong number.
`priced` is true on all three since 2 October 2026. The owner, that day:
"yes price the shining fates, crown zenith and celebrations subsets".
Until then this block was headed WHY NO PRICES and said this repo held no
price for a single one of these 217 cards. That was true of the repo, and
it turned out not to be true of the crawl: PriceCharting files each subset
on its parent's console page, beside the main set, so the pages
sync-pricecharting-cards.mjs already reads every night held all 217. The
block at the foot of that script now matches them on the same row parser,
the same standard-printing allowlist and the same name guard, and on the
first run (cached pages read 23 September 2026) it priced 217 of 217:
Shiny Vault 122, Galarian Gallery 70, Classic Collection 25.
THE PRICES ARE IN data/companion-prices.json, NOT HERE AND NOT IN THE
CHECKLISTS. This block used to say that if prices ever arrived, the right
home was public/data/cards/<set>.json through sync-cards.mjs. The block
below, written the same day, is the reason that is still wrong: those
files are the printed set and ten builders read them. So the subset has
its own price file, written by the same script off the same pages, and
ONLY build-set-pages.mjs reads it. The aim that sentence was protecting,
that the top of a page cannot disagree with the bottom, is kept a
different way: the hero, the chase grid, the value band, the pop-up and
the subset's own list all read one row per card (compRowsBySet).
THIS FILE STAYS IDENTIFICATION. It gained two fields that day:
corpusSet   the set name the printings corpus files the subset under
printed     Classic Collection only. Each reprint prints its ORIGINAL's
number (Charizard reads 4/102, the Birthday Pikachu promo a
bare 24), which no API this site reads carries against the
reprint: TCGdex numbers them CC001 to CC025. Transcribed from
serebii.net/card/celebrations/, read 2 October 2026 (Bulbapedia
refused the request), and HELD TO THE REPO on every build: the
original set is named by apiId and its printedTotal in
public/data/expansions.json must equal the denominator, so a
typo fails the build. It is also the join key: PriceCharting
files Charizard as "#4".
The count check still runs, and a subset marked priced with no entry in
data/companion-prices.json (or the reverse) fails the build too.
Considered and rejected on August 19, 2026, for three reasons that are all
about the reader rather than about the work:
1. The card counts on the first screen are the PRINTED totals. Shining
Fates really is 72 on paper and 73 with its secret rare, and the
collector number on the card in a reader's hand says so. A page that
answers 195 to a card that reads 72/73 has traded one wrong number for
another.
2. public/data/cards/<set>.json is read by ten builders and by
/complete-a-set.html, which prices completing a checklist. Folding 217
cards into three of them silently moves every one of those pages.
3. It could not be done evenly. The Classic Collection cannot be priced
from anything in this repo at all, so folding would have produced two
folded sets and one that quietly was not, which is the exact failure a
reader cannot see.
(Reason 3 is history since 2 October 2026: all three are priced now,
the Classic Collection included. Reasons 1 and 2 are why they still
are not folded in.)

shining-fates.name: the Shiny Vault
shining-fates.what: shiny cards at their own rarities, 104 of the 122 filed as Shiny Rare

crown-zenith.name: the Galarian Gallery
crown-zenith.what: 34 Rare, 32 Ultra Rare and 4 Secret Rare on the checklist

celebrations.name: the Classic Collection
celebrations.what: reprints of older cards, CC001 Blastoise (2/102) through CC025 Tapu Lele GX (60/145) in the card databases' numbering

_noGuideReadme: The same relationship on sets this site has no guide for, keyed by the
companion's own apiId because neither side has a slug. ONLY
scripts/build-expansions.mjs reads this: it is what stops /expansions.html
from tagging three subset rows and leaving five identical ones bare, which
would have taught a reader that Astral Radiance Trainer Gallery is a
standalone set BECAUSE the Galarian Gallery row beside it says it is not.
No guide can be wrong about these, because there is no guide. The row on
/expansions.html carries a name and a card count and neither changes; all
the tag adds is which set the name belongs to, and it links nowhere,
because there is nowhere for it to go.
Found by the same three-way scan the block above describes, run across all
174 expansions rather than only against our 28. sma is the one that no
apiId rule can find: TCGdex and api.pokemontcg.io both file Hidden Fates
as sm115 and its Shiny Vault as sma, which share no prefix at all.
